title: Comparing Lengths and Weights
short: Line things up, or hold them, to see which is longer or heavier.
trouble: Children compare two lengths without lining up the ends, so the one that sticks out looks longer.

blocks.html: You can describe things as long or heavy. Now compare two things directly.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: The left ends are lined up. B goes farther, so B is longer.

blocks.html: To compare lengths, line up the ends. To compare weights, use a balance, or hold one thing in each hand.
When the starting ends match, the one that reaches farther is longer. On a balance, the heavier side pulls down.

blocks.title: Heavier or lighter?
blocks.q: Which is heavier, a book or a feather?
steps: Put one on each side of a balance.
The book is heavier. The feather is lighter.

blocks.name: k-pic
blocks.cap: These ends are not lined up. A sticks out, but B covers 6 spaces and A covers only 5. B is longer.

blocks.html: Comparing without lining up the ends, so the one that sticks out looks longer. It may just start later! Slide them so the ends match before you decide.
For grown-ups: Compare shoes, spoons and pencils by lining them up at one end. Hold two fruits and decide which is heavier.
